key_insight: Inherent randomness in autoregressive decoding imposes a fundamental error floor on length prediction from prefill hidden states, with system error dominating predictor error in the evaluated settings.
engineering_relevance: Inference schedulers should account for irreducible length uncertainty rather than expect more complex prefill predictors to eliminate prediction error.
method: Model decoding as a stopped stochastic process with a time-varying stopping probability.
Derive per-prompt approximate normality, an explicit approximation error, and the affine standard-deviation law σ = αμ + b.
Compare diverse predictor architectures against theoretical error bounds under fixed model, data, and sampling conditions.
evidence_signal: The normal approximation reproduces per-prompt MAE and central distribution mass within a few percent, while evaluated predictor variants achieve similar performance close to the bound.
watch_item: Results depend on model, dataset, and sampling configuration; fix these conditions and report relative as well as absolute errors for meaningful comparisons.
paper_title: On the Fundamental Limits of Prefill-Based Decoding Length Prediction
